title: Release pipeline triggered by version tags
when: The user wants pushing a tag like v1.4.0 to verify, build and publish release files, with the notes taken from the matching CHANGELOG.md section.
prompt:
Goal: A tag triggered workflow that refuses mismatched versions, builds once, attaches checksums and uses the changelog section as notes.
Steps:
1. Trigger only on pushed tags matching v*.*.*.
2. Job verify: strip the v from the tag name, compare with the version in package.json or pyproject.toml, exit 1 with a clear message on mismatch.
3. verify also requires a heading "## [1.4.0] - 2026-10-17" in CHANGELOG.md and runs the full tests.
4. Job build (needs: verify) writes dist/ and runs sha256sum dist/* > SHA256SUMS; upload both as job artifacts.
5. scripts/changelog-section.mjs prints the text between this heading and the next "## [" into notes.md.
6. Job publish (needs: build) downloads the artifacts, gets permissions: contents: write in this job only, and creates the release from notes.md with the files attached.
7. Tags with a hyphen (v2.0.0-rc.1) become pre releases.
Quality bar:
- Published files are exactly the tested files.
- A wrong tag fails before anything is published.
- Humans write the notes in CHANGELOG.md.
Pitfalls:
- Write permission on every job.
- Rebuilding in the publish job, shipping untested files.
- Moving a tag users may have fetched; release a new patch instead.
Verify:
- [ ] Trigger is tags only.
- [ ] Version check exits non zero on mismatch.
- [ ] SHA256SUMS produced and attached.
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md has dated version headings.
Output: the CI workflow file release.yml, scripts/changelog-section.mjs and the CHANGELOG.md heading format.

examples.input: when I push v1.4.0 build the zip and create the release with notes
examples.output: release.yml: verify compares tag and package.json, build writes dist/ and SHA256SUMS, publish with contents write uses notes.md
